summary: Phase A of BUILD PROMPT v4 (WorkCard first-scan flag-gated read-back + idempotency) independently verified. Backend: 4/4 pytest tests pass. Frontend: reload persistence of FIXED card and commit_sha link confirmed live via Playwright on preview. No P0/P1 issues found.

minor.issue: Intermittent 499 (client disconnect / upstream) observed once during project creation load-test; retried and succeeded. Not blocking, but worth noting the upstream can occasionally 499 on this endpoint under load.

issues: Persistent global banner '13 projects point to deleted or unreachable repos — click to clean up' — cosmetic pre-existing issue on this test account, called out in review_request 'ignore' list. No action needed for Phase A.

critical_code_review_comments: backend/routers/onboarding_first_scan.py apply-claim path is well-shaped: find_one_and_update on (fix_claimed_at absent AND commit_sha absent) is atomic; a crashed run_seo_fixes correctly $unset's fix_claimed_at so retries stay possible; a committed run persists commit_sha so subsequent applies short-circuit with already_applied:true. This is the correct idempotency shape.

frontend/src/components/FirstScanCard.jsx read-back logic (line ~226): `const fixed = applyResult?.commit_sha ? applyResult : (state.commit_sha ? state : null);` correctly prefers a fresh session result but falls back to server-persisted commit — this is why F5 keeps the FIXED card visible.
Nit: FirstScanCard has an applyingRef synchronous double-click guard AND the backend has its own atomic claim — good defense in depth; keep both.
Nit: MAX_POLL_MS is env-overridable via REACT_APP_FIRST_SCAN_MAX_POLL_MS — verify production build does NOT set this so the 60s default holds.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase A is proven stable. When testing Phase B/C/D, keep the existing project p_0fdafaa365 as the durable 'already-fixed' fixture — do NOT delete it. The test_admin_001 account has already used its free first-scan, so any newly added project on this account returns status=skipped (this is CORRECT behavior, not a bug). To retest the fresh 'ready → apply → fixed' flow you need a different account or need to wipe first_scan_results.
